reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: Strong evidence - plasma concentrations achieved therapeutic levels (11-23 ng/mL), confirming GSK1120212 reached and engaged MEK1/2. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: No explicit pathway biomarker data reported, but target engagement at therapeutic levels suggests MAPK pathway suppression occurred. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Mixed results - cohort B (BRAF inhibitor-naive) achieved 25% ORR with 4-month PFS, meeting primary endpoint. However, cohort A (prior BRAF inhibitor exposure) showed 0% ORR and 1.8-month PFS, indicating complete failure. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: Clear differential response - BRAF V600E patients (26% ORR) and those without brain metastases (27% ORR) responded well, while prior BRAF inhibitor patients showed no response. This suggests resistance mechanisms develop after BRAF inhibitor exposure. 5. CONFOUNDERS: Single-arm design limits interpretation, but the stark difference between cohorts suggests real biological differences rather than trial design issues.
